issue.description:
## Problem
The repository currently commits only the latest .beads/issues.jsonl snapshot. Full lifecycle history remains in the local embedded Dolt database and is not transparent to GitHub collaborators.

## Required change
Add a supported, deterministic, Git-tracked audit-history artifact and collaborator workflow that preserves issue state transitions without committing machine-local Dolt internals.

## Verification
Prove a fresh clone can inspect the current issues and their published lifecycle history; validate generated artifacts for secrets, local paths, deterministic ordering, and repository compatibility.
issue.notes:
Subagent research and audit findings:
- Beads 1.0.3 supports full-history publication to the same GitHub repository through refs/dolt/data. Fresh clones discover that ref with bd bootstrap --yes before falling back to issues.jsonl. The supported push path is an explicit Dolt remote and bd dolt push; force pushes must be prohibited.
- Fresh-clone audit proved issues.jsonl alone restores current fields, labels, notes, and dependencies but collapses skills-ra5 from 17 native history rows to one imported snapshot and skills-nnz from 12 rows to one. Plain bd init is destructive here: it created an empty DB and deleted the tracked snapshot. Safe setup is chmod 700 .beads, bd bootstrap --yes, git config beads.role maintainer, and bd hooks install --beads.
- bd history is only an issue-table projection: it repeats unchanged rows and omits label, dependency, comment, external-ref, and started-at history. interactions.jsonl and the unimplemented bd export --events path are not valid substitutes. Therefore the design must pair the native Dolt ref with an explicitly limited, deduplicated Git-review projection.
- Transparency and privacy review found zero known secret or local-path pattern matches in the current native issue, event, dependency, comment, and Dolt-log data. Native data intentionally includes Keith Born and keith.born@uipath.com; Dolt root attribution is not useful and is excluded from the projection. All Beads values must be treated as public.
- Hardening recommendation adopted: deterministic history.jsonl, a manifest anchoring artifact hashes to Dolt HEAD, offline terminal-state and append-only validation, recursive decoded-JSON leak scanning, safe bootstrap docs, and fresh-clone recovery proof.

issue.acceptance_criteria: 'bd dolt remote add' (and any other config-mutating bd command that auto-commits) completes without hanging in a repo that has the beads pre-commit hook installed.
issue.description: Running 'bd dolt remote add origin <url>' in this repo hangs forever and must be killed. Reproduced 2026-09-11: the command wrote sync.remote to .beads/config.yaml, then spawned a child 'git commit -m "bd: update sync.remote"'. That commit fires this repo's beads pre-commit hook, which runs 'bd hooks run pre-commit' -> 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl'. The export blocks trying to open .beads/embeddeddolt, whose flock is still held by the parent bd dolt remote add. Parent waits on the child git commit; grandchild waits on the parent's lock. Deadlock. Observed process tree: 54615 bd dolt remote add -> 54624 git commit -> 54626 bd hooks run pre-commit -> 54630 bd export. All four parked in pthread_cond_wait with 0 CPU for 6+ minutes. SIGTERM to the parent alone does nothing; the tree must be killed leaf-first.
issue.design: Any bd command that mutates config and then auto-commits via git is exposed, not just 'remote add' — the trigger is the auto-git-commit step combined with a beads pre-commit hook that re-enters bd against the same embedded database. Candidate fixes: (a) release the embedded Dolt lock before spawning git commit; (b) have bd set an env guard (e.g. BEADS_SKIP_HOOK=1) that the pre-commit hook honors when bd itself is the caller; (c) make the embedded-mode lock re-entrant for the same process tree. Note: the remote registration itself is unaffected — it lands in both .beads/config.yaml (sync.remote) and .beads/embeddeddolt/skills/.dolt/repo_state.json (remotes.origin) before the git step, so the deadlock is purely in the auto-commit tail.
issue.notes: Workaround: the config write completes before the hang, so killing the tree leaf-first leaves correct state. Verified afterwards that the repo had no .git/index.lock, no stray commit, a clean working tree, and the Dolt flock released. Separately confirmed the 'Remotes: origin ... [CLI only]' label in 'bd dolt show' is NOT a misconfiguration: this project runs Mode: embedded (in-process, no server), and 'bd dolt test' errors with "not supported in embedded mode (no Dolt server)" — so there is no SQL-server side to register on and [CLI only] is the expected label.

The manifest was not regenerated when issues.jsonl was resynced in caa107d. 'python3 tools/beads_history.py verify' fails, listing 54 current issues missing from history.jsonl. Nothing wires verify into .beads/hooks or .git/hooks, which is how it drifted unnoticed. (2) The obvious fix re-leaks: 'tools/beads_history.py export' regenerates history.jsonl from the Dolt database and projects historical issue-state transitions, so it reintroduces the raw local absolute path in two skills-37t note transitions — the exact records skills-z8m redacted and skills-wnt ruled must stay out of the readable artifact. Verified by running export (280 transitions, Dolt HEAD 0ntpepkuu6opl8rmp0jlmhvp9r4t59oe) and grepping: 2 hits of /Users/ in the regenerated history.jsonl, both skills-37t, at lines 212 and 214. Reverted with git checkout; tree is clean and the tracked file still has 0 hits.
issue.design: tools/beads_history.py has NO redaction machinery — grep for redact/scrub/sanitiz returns nothing. The 2026-08-14 redaction was applied to the current DB note only (skills-37t's current notes end 'Local absolute path redacted 2026-08-14 for the public-tracker boundary'), not to the historical transitions Dolt retains, and not as a reusable filter. So export is correct about the data and wrong about the policy boundary. This is why the projection cannot simply be refreshed. Options: (a) add a redaction pass to export — a small path/pattern map applied to projected note values, which makes the projection regenerable and lets verify be wired into a hook; (b) rewrite the two historical transitions in Dolt, which skills-wnt already rejected because it needs a force push that policy forbids; (c) accept permanent divergence and stop tracking history.jsonl. (a) is the only option that fixes staleness without either a force push or losing the readable artifact. Note the constraint is asymmetric by design: skills-wnt approved publishing native Dolt unredacted (refs/dolt/data, pushed 2026-09-11, now at 0b95be7e on origin) while requiring the Git-tracked projection stay redacted.
issue.notes: Do not run 'tools/beads_history.py export' and commit the result without checking 'grep -c /Users/ .beads/history.jsonl' first — it must be 0. The Dolt ref is the complete recovery source per the manifest's own projection note, so the stale projection is a readability/review problem, not data loss.

issue.description: The redaction pass (skills-s0g) stops beads_history.py export from producing a leaking projection, but nothing stops a leak reaching GitHub by another route — a hand-edited note, a future bd field, or someone committing a stale artifact. A hook should enforce the boundary at the point of publication. core.hooksPath is .beads/hooks; both pre-commit and pre-push are beads-managed blocks delimited by 'BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION v1.0.3' markers that say not to remove them, so any guard appends AFTER the managed block.
issue.design: Recommend pre-push, not pre-commit, and a narrow leak-only check rather than full 'verify'. Reasons: (1) Publication is the actual boundary — a local path in a local commit harms nothing until it is pushed. (2) pre-commit is the wrong lane on cost and risk: the beads pre-commit hook already runs bd export on every commit, and full verify additionally requires the manifest to match the artifact bytes, so any commit that changes issues.jsonl without a re-export would be blocked — and re-exporting in-hook means 58 bd history calls per commit. (3) Worse, running bd inside a hook is exactly the re-entrancy that causes skills-r0n, so adding bd work to hooks should be avoided. A leak-only guard avoids all of this: it is offline, calls no bd, reads two tracked files, and cannot go stale, because unlike the manifest hashes it does not depend on issue counts. Suggested shape: a 'redaction-check' subcommand (or --redaction-only flag) on beads_history.py that runs just assert_redacted() on both tracked artifacts, invoked from .beads/hooks/pre-push after the beads block.
issue.notes: Full 'verify' in pre-push was considered and rejected for now because its manifest-freshness check couples push to a re-export step; revisit if the projection is ever regenerated automatically. assert_redacted() already exists and is the only piece the guard needs.
